fullPassage: To demonstrate how best to defeat the habit of delaying, Dan Ariely, a professor of psychology and behavioral economics, performed an experiment on students in three of his classes at MIT. He assigned all classes three reports over the course of the semester. The first class had to choose three due dates for themselves, up to and including the last day of class. The second had no deadlines — all three papers just had to be submitted by the last day of class. In his third class, he gave students three set deadlines over the course of the semester. At the end of the semester, he found that students with set deadlines received the best grades, the students with no deadlines had the worst, and those who could choose their own deadlines fell somewhere in the middle. Ariely concludes that restricting freedom — whether by the professor or by students who recognize their own tendencies to delay things — improves self-control and performance.

✅ ① Set Deadlines: A Path to Better Self-Control (정해진 마감일: 더 나은 자기 통제로 가는 길): 마감일 설정(자유 제한)이 자기 통제를 높인다는 글의 핵심을 담음 ←정답
❌ ② Freedom of Choice: The Key to Academic Success (선택의 자유: 학업 성공의 열쇠): 실험 결과는 자유 제한이 더 낫다고 하므로 반대
❌ ③ Why Students Should Avoid All Deadlines (학생들이 모든 마감일을 피해야 하는 이유): 마감일은 오히려 성적을 높였으므로 정반대
❌ ④ The Hidden Dangers of Behavioral Experiments (행동 실험의 숨겨진 위험): 실험의 위험성은 본문 주제가 아님
det.tip: 제목 = 글 전체를 압축. 마감일(자유 제한)이 자기 통제를 높인다는 메시지를 담은 ①이 정답이에요.

ch: Set Deadlines: A Path to Better Self-Control
Freedom of Choice: The Key to Academic Success
Why Students Should Avoid All Deadlines
The Hidden Dangers of Behavioral Experiments

questions.passage: To demonstrate how best to defeat the habit of delaying, Dan Ariely, a professor of psychology and behavioral economics, performed an experiment on students in three of his classes at MIT. He assigned all classes three reports over the course of the semester. The first class had to choose three due dates for themselves, up to and including the last day of class. The second had no deadlines — all three papers just had to be submitted by the last day of class. In his third class, he gave students three set deadlines over the course of the semester. At the end of the semester, he found that students with set deadlines received the best grades, the students with no deadlines had the worst, and those who could choose their own deadlines <u>fell somewhere in the middle</u>. Ariely concludes that restricting freedom — whether by the professor or by students who recognize their own tendencies to delay things — improves self-control and performance.
questions.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 <u>fell somewhere in the middle</u>이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 중간쯤에 위치했다 = 최고 성적과 최악 성적의 중간 수준이었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 성적이 갑자기 크게 올랐다: 급상승이 아니라 중간 수준을 뜻함
✅ ② 성적이 최고와 최악의 중간 정도였다: 정해진 마감일(최고)과 마감일 없음(최악) 사이, 즉 두 극단의 중간에 위치했다는 뜻 ←정답
❌ ③ 학기 중간에 수업을 그만두었다: '수업 중단'은 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ 다른 학생들의 평균과 정확히 같았다: '정확히 평균'이 아니라 '중간 어디쯤'을 뜻함
det.tip: fall somewhere in the middle = 양극단 사이 어딘가에 위치하다. 최고(정해진 마감일)와 최악(마감일 없음) 사이예요!

questions.passage: To demonstrate how best to defeat the habit of delaying, Dan Ariely, a professor of psychology and behavioral economics, performed an experiment on students in three of his classes at MIT. He assigned all classes three reports over the course of the semester. The first class had to choose three due dates for <u>themselves</u>, up to and including the last day of class. The second had no deadlines — all three papers just had to be submitted by the last day of class. In his third class, he gave students three set deadlines over the course of the semester. At the end of the semester, he found that students with set deadlines received the best grades, the students with no deadlines had the worst, and those who could choose their own deadlines fell somewhere in the middle. Ariely concludes that restricting freedom — whether by the professor or by students who recognize their own tendencies to delay things — improves self-control and performance.
questions.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 <u>themselves</u>가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: themselves는 '첫 번째 반 학생들'을 가리킨다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 첫 번째 반 학생들: 'The first class had to choose three due dates for themselves'에서 themselves는 마감일을 스스로 정하는 주체인 '첫 번째 반 학생들' ←정답
❌ ② 세 번째 반 학생들: 세 번째 반은 교수가 정해준 마감일을 받았으므로 무관
❌ ③ 심리학 교수 Ariely: 마감일을 정하는 주체는 학생들이지 교수가 아님
❌ ④ 모든 반의 조교들: 본문에 조교는 등장하지 않음
det.tip: for themselves = 그들 스스로. 마감일을 스스로 정한 것은 '첫 번째 반 학생들'이에요.

questions.passage: To demonstrate how best to defeat the habit of delaying, Dan Ariely, a professor of psychology and behavioral economics, performed an experiment on students in three of his classes at MIT. He assigned all classes three reports over the course of the semester. The first class had to choose three due dates for themselves, up to and including the last day of class. The second had no deadlines — all three papers just had to be submitted by the last day of class. In his third class, he gave students three set deadlines over the course of the semester. At the end of the semester, he found that students with set deadlines received the best grades, the students with no deadlines had the worst, and those who could choose their own deadlines fell somewhere in the middle. Ariely concludes that __________ — whether by the professor or by students who recognize their own tendencies to delay things — improves self-control and performance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자유를 제한하는 것이 자기 통제와 성과를 높인다는 결론
det.analysis:
❌ ① offering unlimited choices(무제한의 선택권을 주는 것): 실험 결과는 자유가 많을수록(스스로 정하거나 마감일 없음) 성적이 낮았으므로 반대
❌ ② removing every deadline(모든 마감일을 없애는 것): 마감일이 아예 없던 반이 가장 나쁜 성적을 받았으므로 반대
✅ ③ restricting freedom(자유를 제한하는 것): 정해진 마감일처럼 자유를 제한하는 것이 자기 통제와 성과를 높인다는 글의 결론 ←정답
❌ ④ ignoring student habits(학생의 습관을 무시하는 것): 오히려 미루는 성향을 인식(recognize)하는 것이 핵심이므로 반대
det.tip: Ariely concludes that ______ ... improves self-control and performance → 자기 통제를 높이는 건 '자유를 제한하는 것(restricting freedom)'!

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 영작하시오. (영어로)
"그는 모든 반에 세 개의 보고서를 부여했다."
[조건] (1) all, assigned, classes, He, reports, three를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 그는 모든 반에 세 개의 보고서를 부여했다
det.analysis: 원문 'He assigned all classes three reports'를 영작합니다. 4형식 문장으로 주어 He → 동사 assigned(부여했다) → 간접목적어 all classes(모든 반에) → 직접목적어 three reports(세 개의 보고서) 순서예요. assigned A B = A에게 B를 부여하다 구조입니다.
det.tip: assigned + 대상(all classes) + 사물(three reports) = 4형식! '~에게 ~을 부여하다' 어순이에요.

questions.passage: The second had no deadlines — all three papers just had to be __________ (submit) by the last day of class. In his third class, he gave students three set deadlines over the course of the semester.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 수동태(과거분사). submit → submitted
det.analysis: 동사 submit(제출하다)을 과거분사 submitted로 변환합니다. 주어 papers(논문)는 스스로 제출하는 것이 아니라 '제출되는' 대상이므로, 'had to be + 과거분사'의 수동태(had to be submitted, 제출되어야 했다)가 되어야 해요.
det.tip: be + 과거분사 = ~되다(수동태). 논문이 '제출되는' 것이라 submit → submitted!

"수업의 마지막 날까지 포함하여"
[조건] (1) and, class, day, including, last, of, the, to, up을 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 수업의 마지막 날까지 포함하여
det.analysis: 원문 'up to and including the last day of class'를 영작합니다. 'up to(~까지)'와 'including(~을 포함하여)'을 and로 연결해 'up to and including(~까지 포함하여)'을 만들고, 그 뒤에 the last day of class(수업의 마지막 날)를 붙여요. of는 '~의'로 the last day와 class를 이어 줍니다.
det.tip: up to and including = ~까지 포함하여(관용 표현). 그 뒤에 the last day of class(수업 마지막 날)를 붙이세요.

questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (10단어) (영어로)
[ an / classes / experiment / his / in / of / on / performed / students / three ]

det.korean: 그의 수업 세 개에서 학생들을 대상으로 실험을 수행했다
det.analysis: 원문: 'performed an experiment on students in three of his classes'. 동사 performed(수행했다) → 목적어 an experiment(실험을) → on students(학생들을 대상으로) → in three of his classes(그의 수업 세 개에서) 순서로 배열합니다. perform an experiment on ~(~에게 실험을 하다), in three of his classes(그의 수업 셋 중에서)로 장소를 나타내요.
det.tip: 동사(performed) → 실험(an experiment) → 대상(on students) → 장소(in three of his classes) 순서예요!

questions.wa: performed an experiment on students in three of his classes
accept: performed an experiment on students in three of his classes

He assigned all classes three reports over the course of the semester. The first class had to choose three due dates for themselves, up to and including the last day of class. The second had no deadlines — all three papers just had to be submitted by the last day of class. In his third class, he gave students three set deadlines over the course of the semester. At the end of the semester, he found that students with set deadlines received the best grades, __________, and those who could choose their own deadlines fell somewhere in the middle. Ariely concludes that restricting freedom — whether by the professor or by students who recognize their own tendencies to delay things — improves self-control and performance.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 영작하시오. (영어로)
"마감일이 없던 그 학생들은 가장 나쁜 성적을 받았다."
[조건] (1) deadlines, had, no, students, the, with, worst를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 마감일이 없던 그 학생들은 가장 나쁜 성적을 받았다
det.analysis: 원문 'the students with no deadlines had the worst'를 영작합니다. 주어 the students(그 학생들) + with no deadlines(마감일이 없는)로 주어를 꾸미고, 동사 had(받았다) + the worst(가장 나쁜 것=최악의 성적)를 붙여요. 'with + 명사'는 앞의 명사를 꾸며 '~을 가진'이라는 뜻이에요.
det.tip: the students (with no deadlines) had the worst. with no deadlines가 주어(the students)를 꾸며요. 마지막은 최악(the worst)!

questions.wa: the students with no deadlines had the worst
accept: the students with no deadlines had the worst
